title: kate-core: complete words from earlier in the buffer
summary: word_completions still lists later matches first. It then lists earlier matches. The word under the caret stays omitted. Duplicates stay removed. Linux CI runs the test.

lane.reason: The work is pure Rust in kate-core. Linux CI runs the test. It does not draw a popup and it does not edit the command.

data_contracts.schema_diff_summary: Keep the word rule, the empty prefix, the zero limit, and the case-sensitive match. Skip the word that contains the caret. Scan later words first. Then scan from the start up to that word. Remove duplicate words. The limit applies to the combined list. A later match stays ahead of an earlier match. The existing prefix test stays green. Leave command.rs, workspace.rs, lib.rs, and keys.rs unchanged. Leave layout.rs and notice.rs unchanged. PKT-0069 owns those files. Leave paint.rs unchanged. PKT-0071 owns that file. Leave fold.rs and view.rs unchanged. PKT-0073 owns those files. Leave command.rs and workspace.rs unchanged. PKT-0074 owns those files. Branch from the current tip of main. base_sha records that tip at planning time. If main has moved, use the new tip.

regression_tests.name: completion::tests::an_earlier_word_completes_when_nothing_follows
regression_tests.asserts: This test fails on main. In alphabet alpha, the caret is Offset(13). The prefix is alph. Nothing follows that word. The result today is empty. After the change the result is alphabet.
